// The C++ of Hostkit.Clock, ported from C# (CodeCoreMorph, D-78).
#include "clock.hpp"

// The C++ of Hostkit.Clock, ported from C# (CodeCoreMorph, D-78).
#ifndef HOSTKIT_CLOCK_HPP
#define HOSTKIT_CLOCK_HPP

#endif

# The C# symbols this port moved to C++, and the C++ that took them over (CodeCoreMorph, D-78).
# One entry per public member of a ported type:
#
#   [[symbol]]
#   csharp = "csharp:Shop.Cart.Add(Shop.Item,System.Int32)"
#   cpp = "shop::Cart::add"        # or a list of names
#   note = "..."                   # optional: what C++ couldn't keep, or why cpp is empty
edits.replace:
# The C# symbols this port moved to C++, and the C++ that took them over (CodeCoreMorph, D-78).
# One entry per public member of a ported type:
#
#   [[symbol]]
#   csharp = "csharp:Shop.Cart.Add(Shop.Item,System.Int32)"
#   cpp = "shop::Cart::add"        # or a list of names
#   note = "..."                   # optional: what C++ couldn't keep, or why cpp is empty

[[symbol]]
csharp = "csharp:Hostkit.Clock.Nanoseconds"
cpp = "hostkit::Clock::nanoseconds"
note = "what the C# does on Linux, clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC); its branch for Windows (QueryPerformanceCounter, QueryPerformanceFrequency) went: the port is built for Linux (D-94)"

[[symbol]]
csharp = "csharp:Hostkit.Clock.MillisecondsSince(System.Int64)"
cpp = "hostkit::Clock::milliseconds_since"

U-0001.summary: Ported Clock to C++: what the C# does on Linux, clock_gettime's monotonic clock; the branch for Windows (QueryPerformanceCounter) goes, as the port is built for Linux (D-94).
